title: The Landlord's Debt
description:
The neighbor grabs {name} and whispers.
"That landlord — I heard he's buried in debt beyond this building too.
Have you checked the registry? Jeonse fraud is everywhere these days."

{name}'s deposit — every won saved over years —
is locked inside that apartment. The phrase 'hollow jeonse' circles the mind.

choices.text: Pull the registry right now.  (fee + time)
choices.result_text: I pulled the documents from the machine at the district office. A dense list of mortgage liens jumped out at me.

choices.text: Surely not. Unsettling, but leave it for now.
choices.result_text:
{name} pushed the thought away. Easier in the moment.
But every night after, 'buried in debt' floated back up and killed the sleep.
Is not knowing better — or is looking away the real poison? No way to tell.

choices.text: Call the landlord. Confront them directly.  (stress)
choices.result_text: It rang three times. The landlord cut me short — "There's no problem at all."

description:
The registry confirms it — the mortgage is at 80% of market value.
If the landlord goes under, not a single won of the deposit comes back.
Luckily, the threshold for lease deposit insurance hasn't quite been crossed yet.

Insurance premium: ₩300,000. More than {name}'s monthly food budget.

choices.result_text:
{name} enrolled in the insurance. The account thinned again.
But that night, for the first time in months, slept deeply.
The price of protecting every saved won — ₩300,000 was cheap.

choices.text: ₩300,000 is too much. Ride it out and hope.
choices.result_text:
Saved ₩300,000. Something for the seed fund.
In exchange, {name} started anxiously checking on the landlord every month.
Whether the savings paid for peace of mind — that would become clear later.

title: Don't Worry
description:
The landlord only repeated 'don't worry.' No real answer.
Got defensive — "How dare you imply something like that."
After hanging up, {name}'s hand was clammy with cold sweat.
Trust them and stay, or cut losses and run?

choices.text: Start looking for a new place before the lease ends.  (moving costs + agent fees)
choices.result_text:
{name} decided to move first. Cost legwork and fees — but better than being trapped in an uncertain building.
Those who want to avoid the worst always move before it arrives.

choices.text: Trust them anyway.  (save on moving costs)
choices.result_text:
{name} decided to believe it. Saved the moving costs and the energy.
But that 'trust' ate a little into the peace of mind every night.
Sometimes the most expensive choice is doing nothing at all.

title: One More Round
description:
Department dinner, third round already. The manager refills {name}'s glass.
"Can't have the new one bailing on us. Drink up, drink up."

Important thing tomorrow morning. Already queasy.
But leaving now means being the one with no team spirit.
In Korean companies, your real evaluation happens at the table, not at the desk.

choices.text: Drink to the end.  (rapport + reputation / health + mental)
choices.result_text: I drained the glass to the bottom. The manager laughed loudly and clapped me on the shoulder.

choices.text: Politely excuse yourself and leave early.  (health / rapport)
choices.result_text:
{name} bowed out. "I have something early tomorrow."
Got home fine. Slept well.
But the next day, the manager's greeting felt oddly cold.
Protecting the body cost invisible points.

choices.text: Fake being drunk. Kill time in the bathroom.  (compromise / risk of being caught)
choices.result_text: I held out ten minutes in the bathroom stall. From outside I heard, "Where'd that kid go?"

title: Next Morning
description:
{name} drank every round to the end.
The manager clapped a shoulder: "That's the spirit — you're one of us."

And then the next morning — head splitting, stomach turning.
The important thing went sideways. The body is lead.

choices.text: Pop a hangover pill and push through.  (show up / worsened health)
choices.result_text:
{name} downed a hangover remedy and showed up.
Shuffled through the day half-dead. Didn't miss work — but the body took weeks to recover.
The price of buying goodwill is always paid in the body.

choices.text: Can't do it. Take a half-day.  (recovery / reputation)
choices.result_text:
{name} filed for a half-day. Spent it in bed.
The points earned last night got trimmed a little today.
You can't have both the rapport and the health — {name} learned that again.

title: Reading the Room
description:
{name} faked drunk and killed time in the bathroom.
Drank less — but nerves were on edge the whole time.
Got back to the table. The manager stares.
"Hey, where'd you disappear to? You weren't trying to run, were you?"

choices.text: Play it off with a grin.  (escape / social energy spent)
choices.result_text:
{name} laughed it off. "The bathroom line was long."
The manager chuckled. Crisis navigated.
Drank less, reputation mostly intact — but it cost nervous sweat.
Knowing how to slip away gracefully is also a skill — and an exhausting one.

choices.text: End up taking another glass anyway.  (rapport / health)
choices.result_text:
Tried to hold out, ended up drinking again.
Drank while anxious, and was anxious while drinking.
Tried to dodge both and lost a little of both — the most ambiguous ending.
